summary: Iteration 5: LIVE trading mode tested end to end against the local signature-verifying Bybit V5 mock (port 8011). Backend: 20/20 pytest pass. Covered: config masking and encryption, POST /api/bybit/test (saved creds, wrong creds giving 424 (10004), unsaved creds), live open through inject_signal (live true, order_id, qty multiple of 0.1, SL/TP and leverage 3 on the exchange), mark/unrealised sync from the exchange, trailing stop pushed to the exchange (breakeven, sl matches the tick-rounded mock value, 'stop REAL movido' log), exchange-side close recorded as a live TRAILING trade with pnl > 0 and a 'CERRADA REAL' log, manual reduce-only close (MANUAL, mock positions empty, closed list grew), close-all {closed:2, failed:0}, guards (account reset 409 and mode paper 409 with a live position; bot start 409 'Modo REAL sin credenciales' after clear_bybit; creds restored and re-verified), mode switch (paper resets to 500 with exchange_synced false; confirm 'si' gives 400; REAL gives live with initial_balance equal to verified equity; mode paper with the bot running gives 409 'Bot detenido'). Frontend: all checks pass: live-mode-badge 'MODO REAL · BYBIT TESTNET', Bybit section with all testids and the 'Verificada' badge, the test-result grid shows Equidad, livemode checklist with 5 items, paper switch (toast, PAPER badge, header paper-mode-badge), go-live dialog (confirm button disabled until 'REAL', reset switch present, toast 'MODO REAL activado', header badge back), close-all button shown with 2 positions and closing both. FINAL CLEANUP done: positions closed, mode paper with reset (initial 500), Bybit creds cleared (env mainnet, base_url ''), bybit_configured false, bot started again (running true, PAPER), mock killed.

minor.issue: Race condition (found in code review, not reproduced). The exchange position list `ex` is fetched once at the start of _monitor_once, without the engine lock, and then the DB positions are read. If open_position inserts a live position after `ex` was fetched but before the cursor reads it, the position is missing from `ex`. _close_live_from_exchange then deletes it locally and records a fake trade while the real position stays open on Bybit with nobody managing it. closed_result can even match an older closed-pnl row from the 60s look-back window. Fix: skip the missing-on-exchange close for positions opened in the last ~15s, or re-fetch broker.positions(max_age=0) (or client.positions(symbol)) before declaring a position closed.

The window starts at opened_at - 60s and the newest row wins. If Bybit's closed-pnl lags after a close and the same symbol was closed less than 60s before this position opened, the previous trade's exit/pnl is used. Filter rows to time >= opened_at, or match by qty/side.
The guard only applies when engine.live. In paper mode, reset deletes every position document, including any leftover live:true ones. Low risk because mode switching requires being flat.
In live mode it only checks that a broker exists, not bybit_verified_at. After the creds are changed (verification cleared), the bot can start live with unverified creds.

6 earlier 'numpy.int64 object is not iterable' serialization errors (jsonable_encoder) logged around 21:31-22:44, before this test run. Not reproduced during this run. An endpoint is returning a numpy scalar somewhere (chart/backtest/optimizer?); cast it to int/float.

issues: 'Cerrar todas' closes all REAL positions immediately with one click and no confirmation dialog. In REAL mode it should ask for confirmation (AlertDialog).
The card stretches to the height of the Bybit card next to it, leaving a large empty area under the 'Volver a modo paper' button (cosmetic).

Restrict closed_result to rows with time >= opened_at (or match by qty/side) so a previous trade's pnl is never attributed
Add a confirmation dialog to close-all-positions-button, at least in REAL mode
Optional: require bybit_verified_at for /bot/start in live mode; find and cast the numpy.int64 value in the earlier serialization errors
critical_code_review_comments: monitor loop: fetching the exchange snapshot without the lock and then iterating the DB can mark brand-new live positions as closed on the exchange
close_position (live) holds engine.lock during network calls plus asyncio.sleep(0.8). close-all is sequential, so N positions block other engine ops for about N*1-2s. Acceptable, but note it.
bybit_base_url is user-settable, so signed requests with the API key can go to any host (admin-only, password-protected; acceptable but worth documenting)
seed_data_creation: None persistent. Mock trades were created then wiped by the final mode reset (paper, initial 500).

The tests leave the system in live mode with the bot stopped, so do the cleanup afterwards. The trailing test sets the mock price to max(entry*1.03, entry+1.1R).
